item.title: Assurance Analyst (Tech) (Rgn) in DIGITAL ASSURANCE & PRODUCTIVITY DIVISION
item.description: Assurance Analyst, Technology Directorate Location: Leeds/London Permanent Full time Flexible Working Options: This role is open to flexible working patterns. These may include: Flexible start and end time to each day. Ability to adapt calendar as needed, for example to fit in the school run, gym or appointments. A 50% in-office attendance requirement that can be spread across the month to accommodate diverse working patterns, such as the flexibility to purchase a weekly train ticket for certain weeks. Working from abroad policy, subject to approval and policy within the team. The Technology division leads and supports all aspects of technology delivery across the Bank, from maintaining critical systems which underpin the UK economy, to providing big data analytics, implementing comprehensive cyber security programmes, and introducing innovative solutions in support of a digital workplace. Technology’s key objective is to support all other areas of the Bank in achieving our collective mission to promote the good of the people of the UK by maintaining monetary and financial stability. This is achieved through the delivery of appropriate, high performing, resilient solutions and information services across the organisation and externally. This role supports the Test Enablement function within Digital Assurance & Productivity Domain under the CTO Division. This function is principally responsible for defining, establishing and forward planning the Bank’s portfolio release & test environment management function. Collaborating with other related functions to coordinate release and test environment activity and to take charge of and own risks. It is also responsible for the process of managing, planning, scheduling, governing and controlling a software release through the different development lifecycle stages and environments; this can include deploying software releases, contention management and working closely with delivery and testing teams as well as the Business. Key Responsibilities / Accountabilities of the Role: Scheduling and planning releases Maintaining and distributing a release schedule Working collaboratively and managing communication with relevant stakeholders Maintaining records and controlling environment usage to support release and change management activities Engagement with Service to ensure Releases follow the Change Management process Co-ordinate software implementations across test (controlled environments) and Live environments Provide input and support for Releases being represented at the Change Advisory Board (CAB) Provide support in collating and reviewing the artefacts required for every release (Release Acceptance Criteria) Provide administration support including arranging meetings, minute taking, documentation, resource request for release, change request closure, record keeping and audit support Minimum Criteria Knowledge of Change, Release and Test Environment Management tools (e.g. BMC Helix, Planview Release & Verify, Jira, Azure DevOps) Written and verbal communication skills for presenting across both Business and Technology teams An understanding of the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) Flexibility (there will be some out of hours and weekend work). Essential Criteria Understanding of Release management Understanding of Project management skills Understanding of Service management skills ITIL Proficient use of MS office programmes especially MS Excel and MS PowerPoint Desirable Criteria Test Environment management skills Planview Release & Verify JIRA/Confluence Source Code Management tool exposure (ideally GITHub) Azure DevOps Understanding of automation and AI Reporting tools (ideally PowerBI or Tableau) Business Proven ability to develop a detailed understanding of the business function relating to the system under change and the stakeholders’ risk appetite, in order to articulate the appropriate design for test environments and data driven from test objectives and the test strategy Occasionally there may be the need to understand complex business processes involving the interaction of a number of systems A general understanding of the Bank’s various responsibilities and how these fit into the Bank’s overall objectives A general appreciation of the Banking and insurance industry Core experience Previous experience working in a service management role Knowledge of change and release management principles and the processes required for supporting them Understanding of the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) Knowledge of test environment management (route to Live) Knowledge of Service Management tool (Remedy, Service Now or similar tool) Personal Clear planning and organisation skills Can do attitude Attention to detail Time management Excellent team working skills Excellent communication and collaboration skills Analytical thinking Problem solving Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. London salary: £33,600 - £37,800 Leeds salary: £30,240 - £34,020 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages. (Amend and add brief details if relevant, such as interview/assessment dates or process for your specific role) This role closes on 05 October 2026 Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Non-Executive Directors
item.description: The National Audit Office (NAO) occupies a unique place in public life. As Parliament's independent public spending watchdog, we help hold government to account, support better financial management and highlight where public services can deliver better value and outcomes. As two non-executive directors reach the end of their terms, we are seeking two successors who will bring independent judgement, constructive challenge and strategic insight to the Board. This is a significant time to join the NAO. Our work reaches across the full breadth of government and public services, informing parliamentary scrutiny, promoting stronger financial management and highlighting innovation across the public sector. One appointee will bring recent and relevant audit practice experience, together with a strong understanding of audit quality, assurance and professional standards. They will be expected to chair the NAO's Audit and Risk Assurance Committee. The second will bring senior leadership experience from the Civil Service or wider public sector, with a deep understanding of government, public service delivery and leading complex organisations at scale. We are looking for exceptional individuals with board-level experience, sound judgement, political awareness and a strong commitment to public service. Successful candidates will help shape the NAO's strategic direction, contribute to its effective governance and provide independent challenge and oversight as part of an open, constructive and collaborative Board. This is an opportunity to contribute to one of the UK's most respected public institutions and to help shape the effectiveness, accountability and value of public services. It is essential that the NAO upholds the highest standards of propriety in its governance. To avoid any conflicts of interest, we are unable to consider applications from individuals who hold executive or non-executive positions within organisations audited by the NAO. Appointments are made by Parliament's Public Accounts Commission on the recommendation of the NAO Chair. Appointments are for a three-year term, renewable for a final three-year term. The recruitment process will include a pre-appointment hearing with the Public Accounts Commission. Saxton Bampfylde Ltd is acting as an employment agency advisor to the National Audit Office on these appointments. For further information about the role, including details about how to apply, please visit roles.saxbam.com using reference OAJXI. Alternatively email maria.dodson@saxbam.com. Applications should be received by noon on Monday 28 th September 2026.

item.title: PA in Insurance ED and Directors Office - Insurance Supervision
item.description: LEEDS BASED Insurance Supervision The PRA's Insurance Supervision Directorate is the largest Directorate in the PRA. We supervise over 500 UK insurance firms and branches of international insurers across life insurance, general insurance and specialist supervision. Insurance plays a vital role in supporting households, businesses and the wider economy, providing financial security and resilience when it is needed most. The sector is grappling with some of the biggest challenges facing society, from climate change and cyber risk to changing demographics, long term investment for growth, and technological innovation. As insurers adapt their business models to meet these challenges, our work continues to evolve too, making Insurance Supervision a fascinating place to work at the intersection of risk, policy, supervision and strategy. We are committed to being a high-performing, inclusive and supportive Directorate where colleagues can build fulfilling careers, develop deep expertise and make a meaningful impact on the safety and soundness of the UK financial system. Role Responsibilities A core part of the role will be the provision of high-quality administrative and business support to the Director of Insurance Supervision, to the Senior Technical Advisor and to the Private Secretary while also being part of the wider office team in supporting the wider ED & Director Office team assisting with in delivering events and key Directorate activities. We're looking for someone who is organised, approachable and proactive, with excellent communication and administrative skills. You'll enjoy managing competing priorities, working at pace and providing a high-quality service, while building strong relationships with colleagues and stakeholders. The role offers a unique perspective on the breadth of work taking place across Insurance Supervision. You'll work closely with senior leaders and colleagues across the Bank, while also engaging with external stakeholders including regulated firms, industry bodies, other regulators and partner organisations. You will be part of a strong and supportive PA community, with opportunities to learn, grow and build relationships across the Directorate. The breadth of the role, combined with the exposure you'll gain to senior leaders and external stakeholders, makes it an excellent platform for future career development. Role Requirements Minimum criteria Experience using the common Microsoft suite of IT programmes such as Outlook, Excel, Word, Loop, CoPilot etc Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. Strong organisational, administrative and time management skills and attention to detail. Proven ability to prioritise effectively and deliver under pressure. Essential criteria Knowledge of the PRA, Bank of England or wider financial services sector. Excellent judgement and decision-making capability. Strong strategic awareness and the ability to connect the dots across complex issues. Strong influencing and relationship-building skills, including with senior stakeholders. Experience of developing and supporting people. Evidence that you can quickly pick up new and complex technical issues. Absolute discretion, integrity and professionalism. Ability to work constructively within a team. Desirable criteria Knowledge of Insurance or Supervision of the Bank of England Experience working in or covering in an ED Office / Private Office An established network across the Insurance Directorate. Understanding of governance, business planning and strategic delivery. A desire to improve processes by using technology to enhance efficiency and ways of working. item.title: Public Affairs and Campaigns Adviser
item.description: Location: Westminster Contract : Fixed term for 6-12 months Salary: £47,609 per annum (Including London Weighting) About us The Local Government Association (LGA) is the national membership body for local authorities. We work on behalf of our member councils to support, promote and improve local government. We are a politically led, cross-party organisation that works on behalf of councils to ensure local government has a strong, credible voice with national government. We influence and set the political agenda on the issues that matter to councils to help them deliver local solutions to national problems. We also provide councils with the tools and resources to respond to challenges present and emerging, and support improvement across the sector. We value diversity and encourage applications from all sections of the community to this high-profile role. About the role Reporting to the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement, duties of the Public Affairs and Campaigns Adviser include: *Work collaboratively as part of the Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement team to contribute to the development and delivery of the LGA’s public affairs and campaigns activity. This will involve working with colleagues across the LGA to enhance the political influence and public profile of both the LGA and local government. *Contribute to the delivery of the LGA’s Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement approach by helping to influence parliamentary debates, select committees and legislation in order to secure positive change on behalf of local government. * Support delivery of the LGA’s Communications Strategy by building and maintaining key relationships in Parliament and with other relevant corporate stakeholders. *Support LGA councillors and member councils to engage with Parliament, including briefing senior LGA members and officials ahead of parliamentary inquiries and as part of the LGA’s party conference engagement. This will also involve working closely with the LGA’s Chair and members of the Senior Leadership Team. *Work with the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement to organise high-impact public affairs events and ensure the LGA has a strong corporate profile at the autumn party conferences. This includes organising high-impact briefings to build the LGA’s network of support in Parliament, supporting the LGA’s annual local government parliamentary reception and organising Smith Square Debates. *Provide perceptive and insightful political intelligence and advice to identify opportunities for the LGA, strengthen the organisation’s public affairs profile and support wider communications activity. *Work with the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement and colleagues across the Communications Directorate to provide public affairs advice and support to member councils, including through the LGA’s Public Affairs Network. * Support the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement in ensuring that the Public Affairs team is the first point of contact for queries from MPs, peers, political parties, parliamentary staff, think tanks and stakeholders on LGA policy recommendations and local government issues. Promote and enhance the reputation of local government and, where necessary, help defend councils’ reputation. *Work with colleagues, as required by the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement, to produce regular forward-looking grids summarising, scheduling and coordinating future LGA public affairs and campaigning activity, announcements and other initiatives. *Undertake out-of-hours duties as necessary, including attending parliamentary, political, think tank and campaign-related events. The position is required to support immediate delivery needs The organisation is consulting on its operating model The grade and responsibilities are subject to confirmation Priority consideration may be given to employees at risk where they have the required qualifications and experience About you Based in the LGA’s office in Westminster, the Public Affairs and Campaigns Adviser will have: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, be highly motivated and able to work using your own initiative. An interest in developing your own networks within both political and communications circles. A strong commitment to personal and professional development achieved by maintaining regular communication with contacts in Parliament, Whitehall and stakeholders relevant to local government. Strong interpersonal skills and a proactive, team-oriented approach to working. A keen interest in networking and confidence to communicate with members of parliament, government ministers and officials, and leaders across local government. Considerable experience working for a parliamentarian, select committee, government department or delivering public affairs in a lobbying/campaigning organisation or within local and regional government. You must have the right to work in the UK, the LGA are unfortunately unable to offer sponsorship visas. Evidence for the right to work in the UK will be requested at the interview stage. Please note that, due to the nature of the role, applications from current serving councillors cannot be considered. To apply If you would like to be considered for the role, please complete the online form and include a supporting statement detailing how you meet the criteria for the role before the closing date. We are specifically assessing candidates against the following criteria: 1. Considerable experience working for a parliamentarian, select committee, government department or delivering public affairs in a lobbying/campaigning organisation or within local and regional government. 2. An excellent understanding of Westminster, Whitehall and local government, including the interface between local authorities, national government, political parties and opinion-formers. 3. Experience and evidence of success in positively influencing relevant opinion-formers, including influencing primary legislation, a parliamentary debate, a select committee report or working with parliamentarians to secure the tabling of parliamentary questions. 4. Evidence of success in working to deliver public affairs plans and corporate campaigns. 5. Experience in aligning public affairs and campaigning activity with colleagues in other disciplines, including media, policy and campaigns. 6. Ability to prioritise competing demands, within a pressured environment, and adopt a flexible approach to work and - when necessary - working hours. Closing Date: 01 October 2026, 5pm Interview Date: TBC We use anonymous recruitment, which is the practice of hiding candidates’ identities. This process involves removing any identifying information from candidates’ applications which includes names. At the LGA we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees where everyone is treated with dignity and respect. Our recruitment decisions are based on fair, open competition, with appointment on merit. ***The LGA are proud to be awarded a “Disability Confident Leader”. Please contact us via *** Recruitment@local.gov.ukif you require a reasonable adjustment, which is a change to the format or conditions of the recruitment process to accommodate any disability-related needs you may have. Our benefits LGA annual leave entitlement is 29 days, rising to 31 days after three years’ service and to 33 days after five years’ service, plus all UK public holidays (pro rata for fixed term and part time contracts).* Flexible & agile working – office-based staff are required to work in the LGA’s London office two days per week as a minimum, subject to business need and this may vary significantly between different roles and from week to week. Future development – face-to-face and virtual courses are scheduled in line with developmental goals The LGA offers 24/7 access to a free, confidential employee assistance programme managed by Health Assured. This service is also available for Dependants. Family friendly policies For more of LGA’s benefits and working with us, please view our webpage https://www.local.gov.uk/benefits-and-working-lga Our values & behaviours Our Values and Behaviours are there to give us an understanding of who we are as an organisation and who we want to be. They are a framework to help us understand: how we work with each other how we work with our members and stakeholders our expectations for ourselves and each other Our values are: Collaboration – We value collaboration, to pursue shared goals by encouraging and utilising diverse perspectives and working with internal and external colleagues across the organisation. Inclusion – We value inclusion, where everyone feels valued, understood, and supported to contribute meaningfully. Ambition – We value ambition, reflecting our desire to achieve best possible outcomes for local government, communities, and individuals. Respect – We value respect, to ensure fairness, recognition, and shared accountability.

item.title: Head of Agentic AI and Data Science Research
item.description: The FCA has retained Global Resourcing to manage this role; send applications directly to Global Resourcing. About the FCA At the FCA, we’re creating a fair and more resilient financial system. We’re establishing more transparent relationships between financial services and customers, building trust in financial markets and protecting vulnerable consumers. We’re currently on an exciting journey as we drive forward significant organisational, people, process, and AI and technology transformation to become a more forward-thinking, proactive regulator. We will use data more effectively to drive better regulatory decisions and build greater cohesion across our broad financial services remit. Significant improvements in digital enablement, business intelligence, market data and information management maturity are all being pursued to maintain our position as a world leader in financial services regulation. In March 2025, the FCA launched a new 5-year strategy to deepen trust, rebalance risk, support growth and improve lives. The FCA will focus on four priorities: Be a smarter regulator; predictable, purposeful and proportionate. The FCA will improve its processes and embrace technology to become more efficient and effective. Support sustained economic growth, by enabling investment, innovation and ensuring the continued competitiveness of the UK’s world-leading financial services. Help consumers navigate their financial lives by working with industry to boost trust, product innovation and ensuring the right information and support is available for people to take financial decisions. Fight financial crime, focusing on those who seek to use the fact they are regulated to do harm. It will go further to disrupt criminals and support firms to be an effective line of defence. The Role The Head of Agentic AI and Data Science Research leads the FCA's capability at the frontier of applied AI, ensuring the organisation not only adopts emerging technologies but understands, shapes and governs them in a way that supports its public interest objectives. Reporting to the Director of Intelligence & Digital, this role is the research and design engine for AI. It provides strategic leadership for AI research, model governance, data science capability, and horizon scanning. It is responsible for identifying how emerging AI technologies can be applied safely, ethically and proportionately to support better regulation, enhance regulatory intelligence, combat financial crime and improve organisational effectiveness. The role owns the FCA's medium and longer-term AI agenda, translating emerging opportunities and risks into actionable strategies, governance frameworks and capability roadmaps. It also leads the FCA Data Science Profession and provides technical thought leadership to senior decision-makers across the organisation and wider regulatory, and technology stakeholder communities. Working closely with AI Product Delivery and AI Security & Technology Operations, the role ensures clear accountability across strategy, research, governance, delivery and operations, without duplication of responsibility. What will the candidate get from the role? Joining the Senior Leadership Team at the FCA during an exciting and challenging time of great change in financial services and its regulation Leading a department of talented and committed people through significant projects whilst also delivering on business-as-usual objectives Exposure to strategic issues and key players in the world of finance, both nationally and internationally Key responsibilities: Lead the FCA's Agentic AI and Data Science Research function, setting the strategic direction for AI research, advanced analytics and emerging technologies Define and shape the FCA's medium and long-term approach to AI and Data Science, ensuring emerging technologies support smarter regulation, regulatory intelligence, financial crime reduction and organisational effectiveness Establish and maintain the FCA's AI governance and research ethics framework, providing the standards, controls and technical authority required for the safe, ethical and proportionate use of AI and advanced analytics Develop and maintain the FCA's medium and long-term AI and Data Science roadmap, translating research, horizon scanning, and emerging technologies into future organisational capability and priorities Lead the FCA's horizon scanning and AI intelligence capability, identifying emerging opportunities and risks, and translating them into strategic recommendations, policy insight and investment priorities Lead the FCA's Data Science Profession; provide specialist AI and Data Science expertise, building professional standards, organisational readiness, and thought leadership while representing the FCA across regulatory, technology, and stakeholder communities Developing and delivering a long-term strategy for the department, aligning to broader divisional and organisational strategies Leading on performance, capability and culture within the department, with a strong focus on operational excellence Delivering through others by relying on coaching, influencing and negotiating skills with a range of internal and external stakeholders Building a strong and inclusive directorate that attracts and develop diverse talent Skills/Experience Required We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer, and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. (To learn more about the Disability Confident Scheme Click Here ) Minimum Significant experience of managing and influencing senior stakeholders internally and externally Experience leading specialist technical, analytical, AI, data science or comparable multidisciplinary teams within a complex organisation Strong understanding of AI, machine learning, data science, and advanced analytics, including associated opportunities, limitations and risks Experience of developing governance frameworks, standards, operating models or strategic roadmaps supporting the safe, ethical, and proportionate use of AI or advanced analytics Proven ability to translate complex technological developments into practical organisational outcomes, priorities, and investment decisions Essential Experience developing strategic, tactical, and ethical approaches for deploying AI and advanced analytics in support of organisational objectives Proven horizon-scanning capability and ability to convert emerging technological developments into actionable strategies, and business roadmaps Experience establishing AI governance, model assurance, research ethics or responsible AI frameworks. Ability to operate credibly as a senior technical adviser to executive and board-level stakeholders. Exemplary communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skill Experience of role modelling strong leadership behaviours in line with organisational values The ability to inclusively lead a group of talented individuals with a wide variety of professional expertise, experience, and backgrounds An open and flexible management style and the ability to communicate effectively to a wide-ranging audience with different skills and perspectives Desirable Advanced understanding of agentic AI, multi-agent systems, and emerging frontier AI technologies. Experience within financial services, regulation or another highly regulated environment. Evidence of recognised thought leadership within AI, data science, or advanced analytics. Experience representing an organisation externally on AI strategy, governance, or innovation topics. Familiarity with commercially available agentic AI platforms and tooling. The FCA’s Values & Diversity Our ambition is to create a diverse and inclusive workplace that reflects the society we serve, helping us to be a better regulator. We serve the public and our decisions directly affect the wellbeing of people, businesses and the UK economy. So, our values matter. They represent the culture we aspire to every day, guiding our judgements, building trust and helping us to be ‘At our best’. The FCA is committed to achieving greater diversity across all levels of our organisation. Given this, we particularly welcome applications from women, disabled, and minority ethnic candidates, as under-represented groups. item.title: Application Support Analyst, Audit Technology Services
item.description: Job description Contract type: Permanent Location: London or Newcastle Salary: c.£50,479 (London), c.£42,778 (Newcastle) a higher base may be considered for an exceptional candidate Office attendance: The NAO operates a hybrid working policy where staff are expected to be in the office a minimum 2 days a week. Main purpose of the job: The National Audit Office (NAO) has made a strategic investment in audit technology and automation to enhance audit quality, efficiency, and value for money. This role provides application support for business-critical audit systems, helping to keep services reliable, secure and effective for auditors. The postholder will support day-to-day operations, controlled system change and service improvement. The role helps ensure audit technology supports audit delivery while meeting NAO security, privacy and governance requirements. As an Application Support Analyst, you will support specialist audit applications used by around 700 financial audit users. These are core business systems, not standard helpdesk tools, and the role is focused on maintaining reliable, secure services, supporting controlled change and improving how the applications are supported and used. You will work with NAO colleagues and third-party suppliers to resolve issues, support releases and upgrades, maintain clear documentation and identify improvements from service data, user feedback and recurring incidents. Key responsibilities: • Provide high-quality application support for users, taking ownership of incidents and service requests through to resolution or escalation. • Investigate application issues, identify recurring problems, support root-cause analysis and agree fixes or workarounds with technical teams or suppliers. • Complete business-as-usual administration, including joiner, mover and leaver activity, access changes and periodic access reviews, ensuring least-privilege access and clear audit evidence. • Monitor application availability, performance, capacity, data quality and service trends, using insight to identify risks and recommend improvements. • Support incident, problem, change, release and knowledge management processes, including controlled configuration changes, maintenance and updates. • Plan and complete functional, regression and user acceptance testing for releases, patches and infrastructure changes, including test scripts, evidence, defect management and post-release checks. • Coordinate supplier support tickets, provide clear evidence, monitor service performance and escalate recurring issues or risks as needed. • Create and maintain support procedures, knowledge articles, user guidance, training materials, service reporting and other documentation to support consistent team delivery. • Support the development and delivery of user training or knowledge-sharing activities where this helps improve application use, reduce repeat queries and support effective adoption of changes. • Support projects and the transition of new or changed services into business-as-usual operation, ensuring support, monitoring, documentation, access, resilience and supplier arrangements are ready. • Participate in extended-hours support during peak periods and occasional out-of-hours work for upgrades, maintenance or priority issues. Skills and Experience Essential skills • Experience supporting business-critical applications or digital services, including incident triage, service requests, escalation and resolution. • Good understanding of application support and IT service management, including incident, problem, change, release, deployment and knowledge management. • Ability to diagnose application issues, identify recurring problems and work with technical teams or suppliers to agree fixes or workarounds. • Experience supporting releases, upgrades or patches, including testing, evidence recording and defect management. • Experience creating or supporting user guidance, training materials or knowledge-sharing content to help users understand application changes and common support processes. • Ability to use service data, ticket trends, user feedback and reporting tools to monitor performance, identify risks and support continuous improvement. • Good data and analysis skills, including intermediate Excel skills and the ability to present information clearly for operational reporting and decision-making. • Awareness of access management, information security and data protection, including least-privilege access and clear audit evidence. • Familiarity with ITIL principles or equivalent service management practices Desirable skills • Understanding of Dynamics 365, Microsoft Power Platform and Dataverse would be an advantage, particularly where these support configuration, application administration, data management, workflow automation, integration and service support. • Familiarity with SharePoint, Azure DevOps and SQL. • Awareness of Application Insights and experience of setting up or using performance monitoring would be an advantage, particularly to support service reliability, issue investigation and continuous improvement. • Interest in emerging technologies, including automation and AI, and how these may potentially support audit technology services in the future. Abilities • Delivers high-quality customer service and a positive user experience. • Communicates clearly and effectively with users and stakeholders. • Able to work at pace, prioritise effectively, and manage multiple issues or tasks. • Works confidently with third-party suppliers, escalating issues appropriately. • Collaborates effectively with colleagues across different teams and seniority levels. • Applies logical, solutions-focused thinking to resolve problems. Out of Hours and Peak Period Working During the peak financial audit period (May, June and July), the postholder will be required to participate in an extended hours support rota. Shifts may fall between 8:00am and 7:00pm Monday to Friday, and between 10:00am and 4:00pm on Saturdays and Sundays, allocated fairly across the team via a planned rota. In addition, the postholder may occasionally be required to work out of hours to support system upgrades, planned maintenance or priority issues where service continuity is essential. Where you are required to work extended or out of hours shifts, you will receive overtime payments in line with NAO policy. To apply candidates should provide: -An up-to-date CV -A covering letter of no more than 2 pages clearly demonstrating how you meet the essential criteria and providing relevant examples from your experience The closing date for applications is 23:59 on Monday 28th September Please note that we reserve the right to close this vacancy early if a high volume of applications is received. Selection process Shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend an initial Teams interview during WC 12th of October, followed by panel interview during WC 19th October or 26 October. Nationality Requirements: -UK nationals -nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK -nationals from the EU, EEA or Switzerland with (or eligible for) status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) Please note, we are not able to sponsor work visas. Please contact us at hrservicedesk@nao.org.uk should you have any questions on your nationality eligibility. Equal opportunities and diversity Disability and Reasonable Adjustments: Applicants with a disability who wish their application to be considered under the Disability Confident scheme should confirm this when submitting their application. Under this scheme we guarantee an interview to an applicant with a disability who meets the minimum requirements for the role. You should also let our HR team know if you wish us to consider any Reasonable Adjustments at any stage of the process (HR Service Desk ( HRServiceDesk@nao.org.uk ). We are committed to fair and open recruitment. All applications will be assessed on merit against the requirements of the role. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected characteristic as defined by the Equality Act 2010.

item.title: Junior Developer
item.description: Job description Contract type: Permanent Location: London or Newcastle with a minimum of 2 days per week in the office in line with our hybrid working policy. Salary: London Salary -c£ 45,316; Newcastle: Salary- c£ 38,403 more may be available for exceptional candidates Role overview The National Audit Office (NAO) is the UK’s independent public spending watchdog. We support Parliament in holding government to account and help improve public services through high-quality audit, analysis and insight. Our work is influential, evidence-based and focused on improving value for money for the taxpayer. The NAO welcomes applications from everyone. We value diversity in all its forms and are committed to creating an inclusive culture in which all colleagues can develop and maximise their potential. We support flexible working and are happy to discuss working arrangements with candidates at application stage. Main purpose of the role The Junior Developer will join AI, Data and Analytics Team (AIDA) to help design, build, test and maintain digital tools that support financial audit work across the Financial Audit service line. The role will contribute to the development of business-critical applications, data products and automation that help audit teams work efficiently, consistently and securely. This is a development role for someone with some practical coding experience, typically gained through 1–3 years in a development, data or technical role. The successful candidate will be able to work independently on defined coding tasks, while also collaborating with developers, analysts, testers and audit specialists to turn user needs into reliable, maintainable and well-documented solutions. Main responsibilities -Develop, maintain and improve applications, scripts and tools that support financial audit delivery. -Write clear, reliable and maintainable code, following agreed team standards and good development practice. -Support the development of front-end and back-end components, including user interfaces, APIs and data processing logic. -Work with structured and semi-structured data, helping to prepare, transform, validate and analyse data for use in audit tools. -Assist with testing, quality assurance and defect resolution, including documenting test results and maintaining an audit trail. -Collaborate with colleagues to understand user requirements, translate them into development tasks and deliver outputs to agreed timescales. -Contribute to documentation, user guidance, technical notes and handover materials so that applications can be supported effectively. -Learn new tools, frameworks and development approaches as AIDA’s technology stack evolves. Relationships and Accountability The role will sit within AIDA and report to the development lead within the team. The postholder will work closely with other developers, analysts, testers, audit teams, and colleagues responsible for technology, infrastructure and digital services across the NAO. They will be expected to work collaboratively, raise issues early and contribute to a professional team culture focused on quality, learning and delivery. Essential criteria assessed at application sift -Knowledge of Python and the ability to use it to solve practical development or data problems. -Knowledge of JavaScript and an understanding of how it is used to build interactive user interfaces or web applications. -Understanding of programming fundamentals, such as functions, variables, data structures, control flow, unit testing, integration testing and -debugging. -Ability to work with data and apply basic data quality checks, validation and transformation. -Ability to produce clear, structured and concise written documentation for technical and non-technical audiences. Additional essential criteria -Attention to detail and a commitment to developing reliable, secure and maintainable solutions. -Ability to work collaboratively, respond constructively to feedback and contribute as part of a multidisciplinary team. -Interest in the work of the NAO and in using technology, data and evidence to improve public services. Desired criteria -Knowledge of SQL and experience querying relational databases. -Knowledge of R, including experience using R for analysis, reporting or application development. -Knowledge of DevOps practices and Agile methodology, including how multidisciplinary teams plan, deliver and improve software products iteratively. -Knowledge of Git and version control, including branching, committing, reviewing and managing code changes collaboratively. -Knowledge of how containerisation supports the development, testing and deployment of reliable applications across different environments. -Knowledge of cloud platforms and data services, such as Azure, Google Cloud Platform or AWS. -Knowledge of CI/CD practices and how automated build, test and deployment pipelines support reliable software delivery. -Awareness of web application frameworks, APIs or client-server application design. -Awareness of testing approaches, code review, accessibility, security or deployment processes. -Awareness of WCAG accessibility requirements and how to implement solutions within apps. -Awareness of how artificial intelligence and automation can be used responsibly to support analysis, software development and audit work. Attributes -Intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn new technologies and development approaches. -Inclusive and collaborative in approach, with a commitment to treating colleagues with respect, valuing different perspectives and helping create a team environment where everyone can contribute. -Problem-solving mindset, with the confidence to investigate issues and ask for support when needed. -Commitment to high-quality work, including careful documentation and a reliable audit trail. -Flexibility to contribute across different projects, users and technical challenges. -Professional judgement, including awareness of confidentiality, data protection and the importance of secure development. -Drive and determination to overcome obstacles and deliver useful, practical outcomes. What the role offers This role offers the opportunity to contribute to work that matters from the start. The postholder will help build tools used by audit teams across the NAO, learn from experienced developers and analysts, and develop skills in software engineering, data, testing and public sector audit technology. The role will provide exposure to a range of projects, from maintaining existing applications to supporting new tools and approaches as AIDA’s technical capabilities evolve. To apply candidates should provide: -An up-to-date CV -A covering letter of no more than 2 pages clearly demonstrating how you meet the essential criteria and providing relevant examples from your experience The closing date for applications is 23:59 on Sunday 4 October Please note that we reserve the right to close this vacancy early if a high volume of applications is received. Selection process Shortlisted candidates will be invited to assessment and interview starting WC 19 October Nationality Requirements: -UK nationals -nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK -nationals from the EU, EEA or Switzerland with (or eligible for) status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) Please note, we are not able to sponsor work visas. Please contact us at hrservicedesk@nao.org.uk should you have any questions on your nationality eligibility. Equal opportunities and diversity Disability and Reasonable Adjustments: Applicants with a disability who wish their application to be considered under the Disability Confident scheme should confirm this when submitting their application. Under this scheme we guarantee an interview to an applicant with a disability who meets the minimum requirements for the role. You should also let our HR team know if you wish us to consider any Reasonable Adjustments at any stage of the process (HR Service Desk ( HRServiceDesk@nao.org.uk ). We are committed to fair and open recruitment. All applications will be assessed on merit against the requirements of the role. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected characteristic as defined by the Equality Act 2010.

item.title: Senior Manager, Data & Statistics in REGULATORY DATA GROUP
item.description: Senior Manager, Data & Statistics in the Regulatory Data Group Location: Leeds The Data and Statistics Division (DSD) is the Bank’s centre of expertise for the collection, compilation, dissemination, and publication of regulatory and statistical data. As part of this, DSD encourages innovation and promotes quality to support analysis, policy and decision-making by the Bank’s various committees, as well as UK government departments and international organisations. DSD collects data from banks and buildings societies, credit unions, insurance companies, regulated mortgage lenders and mortgage administrators. This is done via nearly 40 statistical collections and over 200 regulatory collections. We cleanse a sizeable proportion of these datasets and publish a large volume of statistical data via our interactive database. We support the Bank’s policy committees and the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) Board. Our data are used in a number of publications, such as the Monetary Policy Report, Financial Stability Report, Credit Conditions Survey, Stress Test Results, FPC Core Indicators, and Quarterly Bulletins. Job description The Division is seeking to appoint a Senior Manager to lead its Regulatory Data Group (RDG). The RDG Senior Manager will work closely with the DSD Leadership Team to support the division’s strategic direction. This is an exciting period of change for DSD, leading and feeding into multiple Data Transformation Programmes and delivery of the Bank wide Data and Analytics Strategy. As regulatory data stewards for the PRA, RDG employs advanced analytics and machine learning techniques to ensure high standards of data quality are maintained and continuously enhanced. This is essential for continued integrity and effectiveness of our regulatory framework. The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring that RDG is strategically positioned, appropriately structured, and equipped with the capabilities required, ensuring regulatory data services evolve to support future operating models, technologies and business requirements to meet the evolving challenges and priorities of the Bank. The Senior Manager will set the strategic direction for the group, drive delivery of key outcomes, and provide constructive challenge to support informed decision-making and continuous improvement. They will act as a credible and inclusive role model for a diverse and highly skilled team, investing in the development, wellbeing, and success of colleagues to maximise individual and collective performance. As a senior leader within both DSD and DAT, the job holder will play a key role in shaping the future direction of the Division and Directorate, contributing actively to leadership discussions, organisational development, and strategic decision-making to ensure RDG, DSD and DAT remain well positioned to meet future business needs. Key Responsibilities • Lead the Regulatory Data Group (RDG), ensuring it delivers its core objective of regulatory data stewardship for the PRA while maintaining the right organisational structure, skills, capacity and capabilities to meet the Bank's future needs. • Manage senior relationships with key PRA stakeholders and represent DSD in senior governance forums for Regulatory Data collection. • Ensure RDG is appropriately structured and resourced, with clear accountabilities, succession plans and capability development pathways that enable effective delivery of current priorities and future strategic objectives. • Review and adapt the Group's operating model, ways of working and resource allocation to ensure RDG remains resilient, efficient and fit for purpose. • Manage RDG's budget effectively and work collaboratively with Senior Manager peers to optimise the use of resources across the Division. • Support and champion the delivery of DAT and DSD strategies, ensuring RDG contributes fully to wider Directorate priorities, projects and transformation initiatives. • Provide strategic leadership and constructive challenge, fostering a culture of continuous improvement, collaboration and innovation. Minimum Criteria: • Demonstrated ability to lead and shape teams with varied work portfolios, ensuring the right mix of skills, expertise and resources to deliver high-quality outcomes against demanding deadlines. • Experience of building and maintaining strong relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, including senior leaders, to influence outcomes and deliver strategic objectives. • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to represent the Division and Directorate effectively at senior levels and with external organisations. • Experience of leading teams through periods of change, including adapting structures, priorities and resources to meet changing business requirements. • Knowledge of data governance, data quality management or data stewardship frameworks. Essential Criteria: • Strong people leadership and line management skills, including experience of building, developing and organising teams to meet current and future business needs. • Experience of workforce planning, organisational design or capability development, ensuring teams have the right structure, skills and capacity to deliver effectively. • Experience of leading staff with significant domain expertise while fostering collaboration, professional development and continuous improvement. • Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving and planning skills, with the ability to align team structures and priorities to wider organisational objectives. • Experience of influencing both internal and external stakeholders and driving change across organisational boundaries. • Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex issues clearly to a range of audiences. Desirable Criteria: • Understanding of regulatory reporting frameworks, prudential regulation, supervisory data, or broader financial sector data requirements. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. This role offers a salary of £83,440 - £93,870 per annum (depending on skills and experience). In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ sect

item.title: Professional Training Advisor
item.description: Job description Job title: Learning & Development - Professional Training Advisor Contract type: Permanent Location: London with a minimum of 2 days per week in the office Salary: London c£32,517 per annum plus civil service pension scheme employer contribution of 28.9% Role overview The National Audit Office (NAO) supports Parliament in holding government to account and improving public services, with a focus on driving long‑term, sustainable performance. As an independent body, we scrutinise public spending to ensure value for money for taxpayers and deliver recommendations that lead to financial savings and better service delivery across the public sector. An opportunity has arisen within the Professional Training team (PTT), and the main purpose of this role is to co-ordinate the different stages of the NAO graduate and apprentice programme, supporting onboarding and the qualification pathway of successful students and delivering strong administrative and advisory support across a range of People processes and areas. The successful candidate will provide relevant advice and support to key internal and external stakeholders in an effective and timely way to achieve high service standards. This post will impact successful delivery of a range of Professional Training tasks and will, therefore, affect the contribution of the wider People Team to the business, customer satisfaction and our performance. Key responsibilities The Learning & Development - Professional Training Advisor will be responsible for delivering Professional Training process and assignments in a prompt, accurate and responsive way to a high standard to meet business needs. This will include: -Supporting all administrative aspects of the ACA programme, such as booking study and exam leave, overseeing and reporting on college attendance and mock completion, processing exam results, and supporting payroll inputs. -Working with colleagues to develop study pathways in line with the NAO’s college timetable. -Providing guidance and support throughout the trainee and apprentices qualification journey. -Working collaboratively within the People team to ensure consistency of service, including providing responses to professional training queries received via the HR Portal in a professional manner and to agreed SLAs, escalating complex issues when required. -Supporting communication and engagement with trainees, keeping internal training pages up to date and dealing with qualification queries, escalating to the Senior Professional Training Advisor or Head of Professional Training where required. This will range from dealing with basic queries about college allocations to sensitive and confidential cases impacting their studies. -Build relationships and liaise with external providers, including our college and institute, to ensure a high level of service is provided to the NAO and that they are keeping abreast of new information or issues that may affect the NAO’s work. -Input data accurately and provide management information using NAO’s systems. Undertake data analysis where required (for example exam pass rate analysis). -Monitor and report on ICAEW regulatory activities to key stakeholders. -Priorities and plan work demands and commitments to ensure an efficient service across the wider People team and to deliver work delegated by the Head of Professional Training and Senior Professional Training Advisor. -Follow policy and processes related to their work package accurately, to identify and implement improvements and efficiencies. -Support our People Deal and goals for diversity and inclusion by championing initiatives. -Complete ad-hoc assignments to a high standard Relationships and Accountability Reporting to the Head of Professional Training, you will work closely with graduates and apprentices, performance coaches, and colleagues across the People Team, Finance, and wider corporate services. You will also build strong relationships with external training providers, including colleges and the ICAEW, to ensure a high-quality service. While the role has no direct line or budget management responsibility, you will operate within agreed Professional Training budgets and collaborate with stakeholders at all levels, including senior management, to deliver an effective and responsive service. Essential criteria (used for shortlisting) -Experience in professional qualifications training and/or Learning & Development, ideally within the professional services, education sector or a training provider -Proven administrative and coordination experience in a fast-paced environment -High level of attention to detail and accuracy in data management -Clear and effective communication and presentation skills -Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including data analysis and reporting Key skills and behaviours -Demonstrated knowledge of Professional Qualification Training, Apprenticeships and Learning & Development. -Ability to plan, organise and administer a busy programme of work to a high standard of accuracy and quality, responding to changes in priorities as required, to ensure that key deadlines are met, e.g., exam data processes, monthly pay runs. -High level of attention to detail, working methodically and accurately to ensure all relevant college, student data details are correct. -Self-starter, using creativity and initiative when seeking solutions. -Communication and presentation skills to deliver challenging messages sensitively -The ability to engage and build relationships with internal and external stakeholders -Ability to work well in a team, adopting a collaborative and inclusive approach -Numerical and Microsoft Excel skills, with an ability to analyse data, produce reports and provide accurate management information, in a clear and user-friendly way. -Commitment and motivation to deliver a high-quality service and proactively seeking ways to implement improvements to processes. What we offer -35 days annual leave, including public holidays -Choice of Principal Civil Service Pension Scheme (PCSPS) or a stakeholder pension scheme Flexible working opportunities -Personal and career development support -On-site canteen and gym -Interest-free season ticket loan -Cycle to Work scheme -Online staff discount scheme -Payment of professional subscriptions, health checks and eyesight tests -Enhanced non-contributory death-in-service benefit How to apply Please upload your most recent CV and a Covering Letter no more than 2 pages clearly outlining your interest and suitability for the role against essential criteria and key skills before the deadline. The closing date for applications is 23:59pm Sunday 4 October Selection Process Applicants shortlisted for interview will be asked to complete an Excel assessment in advance. Interviews will take place in person at our offices in Victoria, London during week commencing 19 October Equal opportunities and diversity Disability and Reasonable Adjustments: Applicants with a disability who wish their application to be considered under the Disability Confident scheme should confirm this when submitting their application. Under this scheme we guarantee an interview to an applicant with a disability who meets the minimum requirements for the role. You should also let our HR team know if you wish us to consider any Reasonable Adjustments at any stage of the process (HR Service Desk: HRServiceDesk@nao.org.uk ). Nationality Requirements • UK nationals • Nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK • Nationals from the EU, EEA or Switzerland with (or eligible for) status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) Please note, we are not able to sponsor work visas. Please contact us at hrservicedesk@nao.org.uk should you have any questions on your nationality eligibility.

item.title: Press Officer
item.description: Job description Job Title: Press Officer Contract type: Permanent Location: London with a minimum of 2 days per week in the office in line with our hybrid working policy. Salary: London Salary -c£42,262 pro rata per annum (more may be available for exceptional candidates + Civil Service Pension) Role overview : The National Audit Office (NAO) supports Parliament in holding government to account and improving public services, with a focus on driving long‑term, sustainable performance. As an independent body, we scrutinise public spending to ensure value for money for taxpayers and deliver recommendations that lead to financial savings and better service delivery across the public sector. We are seeking a skilled and proactive Press Officer to join our Press Team. This role is responsible for publicising the work of the NAO to the media to protect and enhance our reputation. The post-holder will need to be able to understand complex, technical information and turn this into simple and engaging messages for our audiences. They will need to be capable of managing proactive, planned press work but have the ability to react to events and enquiries as well. They should also be digitally aware and experienced at using a range of communication tools and channels. Main responsibilities : -Promoting the work of the NAO to external audiences via traditional and social media: -Write press notices, pitches to journalists, op-eds and blog posts promoting our value-for-money and financial audit reports; -Draft social media posts to promote our outputs, working alongside the design team to develop content for multimedia posts; -Brief journalists across print and broadcast on NAO reports to help secure in-depth, accurate and positive media coverage; -Organise and oversee press briefings and media interviews; -Engage with stakeholders, including Parliament, government departments and audited bodies’ press offices; -Support audit teams and NAO spokespeople to communicate our work externally; -Develop communications plans which help achieve audit teams’ impact and influence objectives with our key stakeholders; -Help prepare spokespeople for media interviews by conducting practice interviews and developing support materials; -Respond to time-sensitive, high-profile enquiries from journalists accurately, by drafting reactive lines to take and briefing NAO spokespeople and the media to protect the NAO’s reputation; -Respond appropriately to questions and comments on social media about our work; -Build relationships with national, local and trade press journalists across all sectors our work covers; -Participate in an out-of-hours press office rota with other team members. -Working with press team colleagues to help deliver a range of tasks, including: -Supporting the senior press officers in compiling and sharing media coverage; -Assisting in delivering internal media training for colleagues; -Maintaining media databases compliantly; -Compiling internal reporting statistics. Essential criteria assessed at application sift: -Demonstrable knowledge of the UK media landscape, including a strong news sense and awareness of the UK political environment -Demonstrable writing skills, with the ability to produce clear, accurate, and effective written communications within agreed timescales -Demonstrable communication skills, including the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with a range of stakeholders and convey messages to different audiences using appropriate communication techniques -Additional essential criteria -The successful candidate should also be able to demonstrate the following: -Ability to translate complex and sensitive information and data into simple language -Experience using digital and print media and able to learn new tools quickly -Able to work under pressure and respond to issues at short notice and out of hours -Effective team player with a demonstrated understanding of other communications disciplines -Proficiency in traditional and social media monitoring -Experience working as a journalist, or in a press office or communications team Desired criteria: -Interest in and understanding of how government works To apply candidates should provide: -An up-to-date CV -A covering letter of no more than 2 pages of A4 clearly demonstrating how you meet the essential criteria and providing relevant examples from your experience The closing date for applications is 23:59 on Sunday 4th October Selection process : Shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend an interview, either in person or online during week commencing 19th October. They will be required to complete an assessment exercise in advance, which will then be discussed during the interview. Nationality Requirements: -UK nationals -Nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK -Nationals from the EU, EEA or Switzerland with (or eligible for) status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) Please note, we are not able to sponsor work visas. Please contact us at hrservicedesk@nao.org.uk should you have any questions on your nationality eligibility. Equal opportunities and diversity : Disability and Reasonable Adjustments: Applicants with a disability who wish their application to be considered under the Disability Confident scheme should confirm this when submitting their application. Under this scheme we guarantee an interview to an applicant with a disability who meets the minimum requirements for the role. You should also let our HR team know if you wish us to consider any Reasonable Adjustments at any stage of the process (HR Service Desk ( HRServiceDesk@nao.org.uk ). We are committed to fair and open recruitment. All applications will be assessed on merit against the requirements of the role. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected characteristic as defined by the Equality Act 2010.
