item.title: Technical Specialist, Supervision in Operational Resilience Hub
item.description: LEEDS BASED UKDT Directorate The UK Deposit Takers (UKDT) Directorate is responsible for the supervision of over 600 UK banks, building societies and credit unions. Its aim is to contribute to a safe, sound and competitive UK banking system through delivering effective prudential supervision. The Operational Risk & Resilience (ORR) Hub is one of the specialist teams within UKDT Specialist Supervision Division, supporting the supervision of operational risk and resilience across UKDT non-systemic firms. The work we do is varied and wide-ranging, including leading cross-firm thematic and firm-specific reviews, and supporting the PRA’s response to operational incidents at firms. We also work closely with colleagues in SRS and the other Directorates across PRA/ FMID on ORR related risks. Job Description The Technical Specialist – Cyber Risk, provides specialist expertise predominantly on cyber risk, but is also expected to support on operational resilience, technology and third-party risk related work across UKDT non-systemic firms. The role supports supervisory teams through firm assessments, thematic reviews, incident response activity and technical advice, helping ensure firms can prevent, respond to and recover from operational disruptions. The role also contributes to the development of supervisory approaches, supports engagement with senior stakeholders at firms. Key Responsibilities Lead cyber risk and operational resilience reviews of regulated firms. Provide technical support and advice to supervisory teams. Support the PRA's response to significant cyber and operational incidents. Lead or contribute to cross-firm thematic reviews and horizontal work. Assess firms' cyber and operational resilience capabilities, outsourcing arrangements and third-party dependencies. Produce high-quality supervisory assessments, reports and recommendations. Engage with senior stakeholders within firms and across the Bank. Coach and develop colleagues, may include line management responsibilities. Role Requirements Minimum Criteria Experience in cyber security, technology risk, operational resilience, operational risk, audit or a related discipline. Experience assessing or managing technology and cyber risks within a regulated environment. Experience conducting reviews, audits, assurance work or risk assessments. Strong analytical skills and the ability to produce clear written reports and recommendations. Ability to communicate complex technical issues to non-technical stakeholders. Essential Criteria Strong knowledge of cyber resilience, technology risk and operational resilience frameworks. Knowledge of PRA operational resilience, incident reporting and material third-party/outsourcing policy. Understanding of technology outsourcing and third-party risk management. Ability to identify key risks, root causes and supervisory implications. Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills. Experience leading workstreams, projects or supervisory reviews. Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes. Strong verbal and written communication skills. Experience coaching, mentoring or developing others. Desirable Criteria Knowledge of technology governance, risk and controls frameworks and standards, such as COBIT, ITIL and ISO 27001. One or more related IT risk qualifications, relevant educational background or equivalent risk management work experience. Knowledge of cloud technology and emerging technology risks. You should not be put off applying if you do not meet all these criteria – we would encourage you to get in touch to discuss if needed. The successful candidate will report to the Senior Technical Specialist. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Salary is circa £65,440 - £73,000. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages. This role closes on 8th Oct. Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Agentic Payments Policy Advisor (12 Months Fixed Term Contract)
item.description: Job Title: Agentic Payments Policy Advisor (12 Months Fixed Term Contract) Division: Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC) Department: Market Analysis and Policy – Payments and Digital Assets Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £62,000 and London £59,200 to £69,000 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via steve.christopher@fca.org.uk . Your internal recruitment contact is Louis Vandenburg via louis.vandenburg@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). The Payments Policy Team is a large and growing team focused on working closely with HMT Treasury, and colleagues across FCA and PSR, to modernise the payments regulatory framework. This includes work realise the benefits of agentic payments, whilst maintaining a safe and trusted payments system Role responsibilities Lead policy work on agentic payments by shaping proposals, reviewing information and collaborating with teams across the FCA Help shape change by contributing to drafting public consultations on FCA rules and guidance, ensuring our priorities align with industry and regulatory developments Engage with stakeholders by building close relationships with government, other domestic and international regulators and industry participants to help shape the future of payments policy Provide specialist insight by delivering advice and briefings on payments policy issues to colleagues and senior management, shaping FCA strategy Grow your skills by developing deep knowledge of payments services and regulations and the risks and opportunities of agentic AI and agentic payments Be part of transformation by playing a key role in a major regulatory change project, working as a team to develop innovative solutions in an evolving policy landscape Skills required Minimum: Prior experience of analysing information and contributing to the development of policy relating to financial services and/or innovative technology Prior experience of presenting key issues clearly and succinctly, both verbally and in writing Prior experience of building and managing effective relationships with a range of stakeholders Essential: Experience developing policy that supports consumer protection, drives innovation and competition, and/or promotes growth and UK competitiveness Effective problem-solving and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes in a fast-paced environment A flexible and proactive approach, demonstrating a willingness to learn, take on new responsibilities, and adapt to changing priorities Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Timeline: Job advert close: 4th October 2026 at Midnight CV Review/Shortlist: 6th October 2026 Interviews: 12th – 20th October 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time

item.title: 12 month FTC PA in ECONOMIC OUTLOOK DIVISION & CURRENT ECONOMICS DIVISION
item.description: Location: Leeds and London Directorate / Division Overview Monetary Policy Assessment and Strategy provides the core analytical support that helps the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) make decisions on monetary policy to meet the inflation target. The area brings together expertise in economic analysis, forecasting and policy strategy, working closely with colleagues across the Bank and the MPC Unit. Within the area, the Economic Outlook and Current Economic Conditions divisions play a central role in assessing developments in the UK and global economy, producing analysis that supports the MPC's understanding of inflationary pressures and the outlook for growth and inflation. We are seeking a highly motivated, organised and proactive Personal Assistant to provide high-quality support to the Head of Divisions and selected senior managers. This is a varied and interesting role in a dynamic area of the Bank, offering exposure to senior stakeholders, divisional management activity and cross-Bank work. The jobholder will provide a full secretarial, administrative and operational support service. They will be expected to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgement, build strong relationships across the Bank and handle sensitive information with discretion. The role would suit someone who enjoys working at pace, takes pride in delivering excellent support and is keen to improve processes and ways of working. The successful candidate will be part of a wider PA and support team. The team is self-covering, so the jobholder will be expected to work flexibly with other PAs, provide cover during absences and contribute positively to the wider support community, including cover for more senior PA offices where required. You would: Provide proactive, high-quality PA support to the Head of Divisions and selected senior managers, acting as a trusted point of contact and using judgement when handling requests. Manage complex and frequently changing diaries, resolve scheduling conflicts, prioritise competing meeting requests and ensure senior leaders have sufficient preparation time. Proactively manage inboxes, monitor correspondence, highlight urgent matters, coordinate responses and ensure actions are progressed promptly. Organise divisional management meetings, leadership meetings and wider staff events, including agendas, papers, minutes and action tracking. Work with the Head of Divisions and management teams to keep the divisions running effectively, highlighting outstanding actions, chasing deadlines and supporting governance activity. Build and maintain strong working relationships with colleagues at all levels, including senior internal stakeholders and external contacts. Support recruitment activity, including arranging interviews, preparing interview packs, coordinating candidate communications and supporting onboarding arrangements. Complete joiner, mover and leaver processes and help ensure colleagues have a positive experience when joining or moving within the division. Arrange domestic and international travel, prepare itineraries, process expenses and support budget tracking or other administrative processes through the year. Identify opportunities to improve, streamline or automate divisional processes, including making effective use of Microsoft 365 tools and new technologies. Work collaboratively with the wider PA network, providing cover across divisions and supporting senior PA offices when required. There is some flexibility to shape the role around the successful candidate’s strengths and interests, particularly in relation to process improvement, divisional coordination and wider PA community contribution. Role Requirements: Minimum Criteria This role requires strong PA or executive support experience, excellent judgement and the ability to provide calm, proactive support in a busy senior leadership environment. ​​ You should have:​ Strong organisational, prioritisation and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Experience managing complex diaries, inboxes, meetings, papers, actions, travel and expenses. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with confidence engaging with colleagues at all levels. Sound judgement, discretion and professionalism when handling sensitive or confidential information. A proactive, self-starting approach, with the ability to work independently, use initiative and solve problems. Flexibility, resilience and the ability to remain calm and effective under pressure. Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Microsoft 365 tools, particularly Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, OneNote and Excel. Essential Criteria A collaborative approach and commitment to inclusive, respectful working practices. Excellent attention to detail and commitment to delivering accurate, high-quality work. Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build effective relationships and networks quickly. Desirable Criteria Experience of having supported Heads of Divisions or Department level or above. Taking minutes of meetings Basic MS Excel skills. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. The salary for this role is, Leeds: £25,760 - £28,980 and London: £28,640 - £32,220 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages. (Amend and add brief details if relevant, such as interview/assessment dates or process for your specific role) This role closes on 5th October 2026 Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Appointment of Members to the Northern Ireland Fiscal Council
item.description: NORTHERN IRELAND FISCAL COUNCIL BRINGING GREATER TRANSPARENCY AND INDEPENDENT SCRUTINY TO THE CURRENT AND FUTURE CONDITION OF NORTHERN IRELAND’S PUBLIC FINANCES. Appointment of Members The Department of Finance is seeking to appoint up to three new members for the Northern Ireland Fiscal Council. The terms of appointment will be for five years. The aim of the Council is to bring greater transparency and independent scrutiny to the current and future state of Northern Ireland’s public finances, to inform public debate, and policy decisions. It provides independent reporting on the Executive’s performance in delivering its budget. Members are appointed by the Finance Minister for their independence and expertise, and are expected to act impartially, free from political influence. They should be willing and able to engage with Assembly Committees, contribute to public discussion, and speak at events on matters relating to public finances. The appointments come at an exciting time for the Council which having been formed in 2021, has recently gone through the Assembly process to place it on a statutory footing. Members of the Council will require a commitment of up to 30 days per annum to the appointment. This position will be paid at a rate of £390 per day. The appointment is non-pensionable. How to Apply For more detailed information on the role and person specification, please click on the 'Candidate Information Booklet' link below. In order to apply for this position, please click on the 'Apply for this job online' link below to register to this vacancy and to submit an online application. Alternatively you can request an application pack by contacting: HRConnect, PO Box 1089, Beacon House, 27 Clarendon Road Belfast BT1 9EX. Telephone: 0800 1 300 330. Email: recruitment@hrconnect.nigov.net All requests must include your name, address and reference number IRC330471. The application pack can also be requested in alternative formats by contacting HRConnect. Reasonable adjustments will be made to accommodate the needs of those with a disability. Completed application forms must be returned to arrive not later than 12:00 noon (UK time) on Friday 9th October 2026. Applicants invited for interview are eligible for reimbursement of reasonable travelling expenses incurred within Europe. It is anticipated that interviews will be held in Colby House, Stranmillis Court, Stranmills Road, Belfast BT1 9RR on 14 and 15 December 2026. Equality of Opportunity : The Department is committed to the principle of public appointments based on merit with independent assessment, openness and transparency of process. The Department is also committed to equality of opportunity and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified applicants irrespective of religious belief, gender, race, political opinion, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, or whether or not they have dependents. As those with disabilities and women are underrepresented, applications from these sections of the community would be particularly welcome.

item.title: Security Supervisor in Security Ops London
item.description: Location: Threadneedle Street and Moorgate, with deployment to other Bank locations where required Working arrangement: Fully site-based operational role Working pattern: Monday to Friday, eight hours per day inclusive of a one-hour break. Occasional attendance outside normal hours may be required for planned training, exercises, or significant operational needs, in accordance with contractual terms and Bank policy. Reports to: Designated Security Shift Manager Supervisory responsibility: Day-to-day supervision of a designated security cohort, currently approximately 20 personnel About the role Security Operations is responsible for protecting the Bank’s people, buildings, assets, information, and operations. Working across a complex and high-profile estate, the function contributes to the Bank’s operational resilience and its responsibilities as part of the UK’s Critical National Infrastructure. As a Security Supervisor, you will provide visible frontline leadership and oversee the safe, professional, and effective delivery of security operations. Your primary responsibility will be the day-to-day supervision of a designated Monday-to-Friday security cohort and associated public-facing, access-control, and external-interface activities. You will allocate duties, maintain operational standards, support officer welfare and development, coordinate resources and make proportionate tactical decisions within your delegated authority. To maintain operational flexibility, you may also supervise or support wider Security Operations activity across Bank locations where you are appropriately trained, competent, and authorised. This is a frontline supervisory role. Security Managers retain accountability for overall operational command, rostering, workforce planning, strategic direction, significant changes to operating arrangements and formal employee-relations decisions. Key responsibilities You will: Provide visible leadership and day-to-day supervision to in-house security personnel. Coordinate public-facing security, access control, screening, searches, vehicle, and delivery activity, guarding, and patrols. Translate management priorities into clear briefings, instructions, and operational tasking. Allocate duties, monitor post coverage, and maintain accurate information on personnel locations and operational commitments. Ensure personnel maintain high standards of vigilance, conduct, appearance, customer service, and procedural compliance. Respond to incidents, alarms, and emergencies, making timely and proportionate tactical decisions within delegated authority. Initiate approved security and emergency procedures, coordinate available resources, and maintain effective communication until responsibility transfers to a Security Manager or the emergency services. Ensure incidents, decisions, handovers, and operational activity are recorded and escalated appropriately. Address immediate concerns relating to standards, conduct or performance through instruction, feedback, and coaching, escalating serious or repeated concerns through the appropriate management arrangements. Support day-to-day attendance, sickness, welfare, and development matters within the boundaries of the role. Conduct proportionate checks of posts, equipment, records and operational delivery, supporting audits, exercises, and assurance activity. Deliver operational briefings and task-specific instruction, identify training needs, and communicate learning from incidents and exercises. Apply security controls firmly, consistently, proportionately, and respectfully. Build effective working relationships with Bank colleagues, contracted security providers, visitors, contractors, senior stakeholders, emergency services, and external security partners. Contribute frontline knowledge and operational feedback to reviews and service improvements. Operational scope Your duties may include: Access control and identity verification Perimeter, reception, and front-of-house security Vehicle access, deliveries, and screening Personal, property, vehicle, and building searches X-ray and other screening activities Static guarding and patrols Security Control Room operations Monitoring CCTV, access-control, alarm, fire, and communication systems Event and incident support Responses to security, fire, and medical emergencies Specialist or unfamiliar duties will only be undertaken where the necessary training, competence, equipment, and authority are in place. About you Minimum criteria You must be able to demonstrate: Experience supervising or leading personnel in a security or comparable operational environment. Experience responding to incidents and implementing emergency procedures. Clear verbal and written communication skills. The ability to work the stated Monday-to-Friday pattern and across Bank locations as required. Essential criteria You will also need: The ability to provide visible frontline leadership and clear operational direction. Strong situational awareness, sound judgement, and proportionate decision-making under pressure. The ability to coordinate resources, manage competing priorities and escalate shortfalls or risks promptly. Experience addressing operational standards, conduct and performance through instruction, coaching, and appropriate escalation. The ability to support attendance, welfare, and staff development within defined supervisory boundaries. Good working knowledge of access control, searches, screening, patrols, guarding, and building-security operations. Competence in relevant security technology, including CCTV, access-control, alarm, fire, communication, and screening systems. The ability to operate effectively in a Security Control Room environment, assess information, maintain accurate records, coordinate responses, and escalate incidents. A professional, customer-focused approach and the confidence to engage with a wide range of stakeholders. High standards of integrity, discretion, professionalism, and personal accountability. The flexibility to support wider Security Operations activity within the remit of the role. Desirable criteria It would be beneficial to have: Experience in Critical National Infrastructure, financial services, government, or another high-security environment. Experience supervising both in-house and contracted security personnel. Relevant security, Control Room, first-aid, incident-management, or screening qualifications. Experience supporting operational training, exercises, assurance activity, or post-incident reviews. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Location London Sites - This role offers a salary of £33,600 - £37,800 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see you

item.title: Financial Crime Data Analyst
item.description: Job Title: Financial Crime Data Analyst Division: Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC) Department: Financial Crime Markets (FCMI) Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £43,100 to £48,000 and London £47,300 to £53,000 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Associate – Level 8 – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via steve.christopher@fca.org.uk . Your internal recruitment contact is Isabelle Groves via isabelle.groves@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition. The Financial Crime Market Intervention department, within the Specialist Directorate, provides specialist expertise to help reduce the risk that regulated businesses are used for financial crime. The department includes four Financial Crime Specialist Supervision teams, a Sanctions Supervision Team, a Fraud Supervision Team and a Risk, Data and Strategy Team. Working with colleagues across the FCA and external partners, it focuses on money laundering, financial sanctions, fraud, bribery and corruption. This role sits in the Risk, Data and Strategy Team. Role responsibilities Help shape innovative data-led approaches that enhance the FCA’s ability to prevent and detect financial crime, protecting consumers and markets across the UK Turn complex data into clear, actionable insights that support supervisory decisions and drive meaningful regulatory outcomes Collaborate with colleagues across Data and Supervision to deliver impactful projects that enhance the FCA’s financial crime capabilities Develop specialist skills in data analytics within a high-profile regulatory environment, building skills and experience that can help protect millions of consumers Skills required Minimum: Prior experience using Excel, SQL, or another data analytics tool to interrogate and manipulate data Prior experience analysing data to answer defined questions and draw practical conclusions Prior experience presenting analysis clearly in written, visual, or verbal formats Essential: Effective communication skills, with the ability to explain data analysis and insights clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences Ability to deliver high-quality work to tight deadlines, using initiative and sound judgement Well-developed stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build effective relationships, provide constructive challenge and confidently engage with senior stakeholders Ability to prioritise competing demands and manage multiple pieces of work with minimal supervision A collaborative and forward-thinking approach, demonstrating curiosity, innovation and a positive attitude to problem-solving Confidence in making informed judgements, taking timely decisions and learning from experience to continuously improve outcomes Experience creating data visualisation dashboards (e.g. Tableau), analytical programming languages (e.g. Python, R or advanced SQL) and knowledge of financial services, regulation, financial crime, or supervisory data is desirable Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Timeline: Job advert close: 30th September 2026 at Midnight CV Review/Shortlist: 2nd - 6th October 2026 Interviews w/c 19th October 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time .

item.title: Strategic Assessment Intelligence Analyst – FTC until 31/03/28
item.description: Strategic Assessment Intelligence Analyst – FTC until 31/03/28 Division: Enforcement and Market Oversight Department : Enforcement Intelligence and Specialist Services · Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £59,600 and London from £59,200 to £65,000 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) · This role is graded as: Senior Associate - Regulatory · Your recruitment contact is Riley Fox via riley.fox@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. Sitting within the Enforcement & Market Oversight Division, the Enforcement Intelligence and Specialist Services (EISS) Directorate provides strategic knowledge, intelligence capabilities, and operational support across enforcement functions, improving the FCA’s ability to detect harm, deliver effective investigations, and uphold market integrity. The FCA has recently built a strategic analysis function within the Specialist Intelligence Department (SID) to understand, support and progress the FCA’s operational objectives. The FCA strategy between 2025-2030 commits to 4 key objectives, one of which is preventing Financial Crime, and this function within the Partner & Insights team is central to achieving this objective The strategic assessment team provides a unique insight into the financial crime threats the FCA and our regulated populations are exposed to, offering all-source analysis to better understand new threats and emerging issues and offer robust recommendations to internal stakeholders to better mitigate the threat of harm. Role responsibilities · Conducting strategic analysis of internal and external threats, including scanning, across the financial crime landscape to support informed decision-making for FCA seniors. · Contextualising and summarising a wide range of intelligence sources to inform analysis. · Identifying emerging threats, risks and vulnerabilities through comprehensive analysis to guide strategic and tactical prioritisation. · Developing and delivering strategic assessments and intelligence reports tailored to internal stakeholder requirements, as well as adapting such assessments for external partner awareness. · Generating and gathering all-source intelligence to detect and understand financial crime threats such as money laundering, fraud, AI, digital assets, technological advancements and sanctions evasion affecting the UK financial services sector. · Creating high-quality analytical products tailored to diverse audiences, using appropriate formats and presentation styles to communicate insights effectively · Collaborating with internal stakeholders and external partners to enhance threat understanding, share methodologies and review analytical outputs. · Building and maintaining regular proactive relationships with the analytical community, including identifying opportunities to collaborate on multi-agency threat assessments that have wider impacts on multiple sectors, the UK and worldwide. Skills required Minimum: · Minimum of SC clearance is required - DV clearance (or a willingness to undertake DV clearance) is advantageous. · Prior experience, and demonstrable ability to analyse complex intelligence and data from diverse sources to draw sound, evidence-based conclusions with clear and effective communication of findings both verbally and in writing - experience to include producing strategic intelligence assessments. · Demonstrated experience in effectively managing internal stakeholder and external partner relationships Essential: · Effective written and verbal communication skills, including proficiency in Microsoft packages. · Demonstrable understanding of the digital assets sector and the relevant economic crime threats, including how harm can be mitigated. · Skilled in delivering analytical insights across grades. · Experience of working collaboratively in cross-functional teams to deliver intelligence-led projects to progress customer needs. · Well-versed in the financial services sector and/or UK Economic Crime landscape including current national priorities. · Demonstrable application of National Intelligence Model principles and relevant intelligence and information sharing frameworks. · Solid understanding of UK Government, Law Enforcement, Regulatory and private sector structures, functions and role. · Understanding and application of the PHIA Common Analytical Standards. Benefits · 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays · Hybrid model where Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices · Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary · Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance · 35 hours of paid volunteering annually · A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values & culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability Confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes, we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timeline · Advert Closing: 4 October at 11:59pm · CV Review/Shortlist: 6 October · Case Study Assessment: 12-13 October · Interviews: w/c 26th October · Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time. · SC Clearance is required for this role ( SC Guidance ) - you will hold or will be required to obtain Security Check (SC) level vetting.

item.title: Lead Financial Promotion Supervisor
item.description: Job Title: Lead Financial Promotion Supervisor Division: Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC) Department: Consumer Investments (CI) Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £60,700 to £75,600 and London £66,600 to £83,100 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Lead Associate – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via steve.christopher@fca.org.uk . Your internal recruitment contact is Isabelle Groves via isabelle.groves@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). We are currently recruiting for a Lead Associate to join our Engagement & Strategy Team within SPEP. Our department has a broad remit across both authorised and unauthorised activities, working to reduce harm arising from non-compliant financial promotions, scams, fraud, high-risk investments and other activities that may lead to consumer harm or financial loss. The Engagement & Strategy Team plays a critical role in identifying and assessing emerging risks through horizon scanning, risk analysis and strategic project work. The team oversees the department’s risk framework and project portfolio, helping to shape proactive interventions that mitigate harm, support market integrity and deliver better outcomes for consumers across the UK. Role responsibilities Lead high-profile supervisory projects, delivering robust analysis and evidence-based assessments that help shape regulatory outcomes and protect consumers Identify emerging and complex risks across financial markets, assessing potential harm and supporting action to improve outcomes for people and businesses across the UK Apply intelligence, data and cross-FCA collaboration to spot issues early, helping to prevent consumer and market harm before it occurs Evaluate innovative and higher-risk financial promotions, including cryptoassets and non-mainstream investments, applying regulatory expertise to support sound decision-making Help create positive change by developing creative approaches to reducing harm, working with firms to raise standards and deliver better consumer outcomes Coach, support and develop colleagues while helping to shape team priorities, ensuring resources are focused on the areas that deliver the greatest impact for consumers and markets Skills required Minimum: Prior experience of making timely, risk-based decisions, with clear justification and the ability to implement an appropriate strategy Prior experience in analysing complex information from multiple sources to identify key risks, insights and outcomes Prior experience of supporting, mentoring and leading others, delivering results through collaboration and communicating clearly and concisely Essential: Demonstrated accountability, with the ability to take ownership of issues and deliver pragmatic, solutions-focused outcomes Solid organisational and prioritisation skills, with the ability to manage competing demands and adjust to changing priorities Effective influencing and negotiation skills, while maintaining the integrity and accuracy of key messages and issues Sound judgement, with the ability to assess, analyse and validate risks, reaching robust and well-reasoned decisions in demanding situations Ability to work well collaboratively as part of a team to meet shared objectives and deliver effective outcomes Well-developed written and verbal communication abilities, including the capacity to convey complex ideas clearly and confidently to different audiences Commitment to continuous learning and development, with a flexible, adaptable and proactive approach to taking on new responsibilities Ability to build and maintain positive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders at all levels to support the delivery of organisational objectives Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Timeline: Job advert close: 9th October 2026 at Midnight CV Review/Shortlist: 13th October 2026 Case Study Assessment & Interviews: w/c 19th October 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time

item.description: Internal Audit Internal Audit (IA) assists the Court of Directors and Executive Management in protecting the Bank’s assets, reputation, and sustainability. It does this by independently and objectively evaluating the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management and governance processes. As part of this assurance, IA provides advice, insight and foresight and recommends cost-effective improvements, including efficiencies, which are agreed with management and tracked until implementation. Internal Audit (IA) acts as the third line of defence within the Bank and currently has c. 25 professional staff. The Directorate reports directly to the Audit and Risk Committee (ARCo) through the Audit Director and works closely with the Bank’s external auditors, the Treasury as well as other European banks. Each year, we present our audit plan to ARCo for the year ahead that sets out the audits we will complete in the year ahead. As well as completing the audits in the plan, we also engage in continuous monitoring, provide input to Bank-wide projects and complete unplanned work, usually at the request of ARCo. Based on our audit work, we make cost-effective recommendations to management that are designed to improve the Bank's control environment. Job Description The Internal Audit Directorate has a vacancy for a Lead Auditor. The ability and desire to drive positive change is central to the Bank's remit and you will be passionate about making a real difference to the Bank’s controls and business processes. With limited direct supervision from an Audit Manager, you will be required to: form relationships with management and staff across the Bank; develop a keen understanding of the business; and plan and perform audits in all areas of the Bank as required. Role Accountabilities The role requires the role holder to: Gain an understanding of the Bank and its evolving role in the UK financial system to be able to identify the risks facing the Bank and to inform the planning of specific audits. Investigate everything from the effectiveness of controls through to behaviour and culture. Ensure completion of all audit work within allocated time and budgets. Articulate conclusions and formulate cost-effective recommendations. Voice independent opinions underpinned by objective analysis. Write precise and readable audit reports that clearly convey key messages to senior stakeholders. Challenge management constructively to ensure they take appropriate action. Collaborate closely with the business in tracking progress in addressing audit recommendations and confirming their closure. Provide input into often high-profile projects across the Bank. Support the development of departmental standards and audit methodology. Work efficiently across audits and supporting processes, improving and sharing practices to strengthen Directorate delivery. Role model the Bank’s behaviours at all times; Acting Inclusively, Driving Growth and Delivering Outcomes. Minimum Criteria Ability to identify, recommend and drive through practical, cost-effective control improvements. Excellent attention to detail, ensuring that outputs are accurate and supportable the first time. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to express views clearly and encourage open discussion. Able to balance multiple priorities and deliver within pre-agreed timelines. Essential Criteria Comfortable building business relationships and collaborating closely with senior management and external stakeholders. Demonstrable experience of working both independently and within a team and delivering high quality work to deadlines. Desirable Criteria Working level experience of conducting audit, risk or compliance reviews. Accountancy or audit qualification. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. This role offers a salary as follows: Leeds circa £46,320 - £52,110 London circa £51,440 - £64,300 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages. This role closes on 15 October 2026. Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Senior Security Analyst in Security Ops - London
item.description: Location: London, Scale G, Permanent position, Personal Security and Safety Analyst , Security Ops. Division Overview The Security division within the Bank mitigates risks to the Bank’s property, infrastructure, people, services or assets being compromised, harmed, damaged, stolen or disrupted either by external actors and or people exploiting their access to Bank assets or premisses. The Team This role sits within the Personnel Security function of the Bank, protecting the Bank and its people from insider risk and extending the protection of the Bank beyond its physical buildings. The personal safety and security role plays a critical role in safeguarding employees and ensuring compliance with relevant Bank policies. The role involves assessing, managing, and mitigating risks associated with personal security to the Banks operations and its people. This primarily relates to business travel, including working from abroad. The analyst will monitor global security events, conduct risk assessments, and provide guidance to protect travellers and maintain operational continuity. It also includes the investigation and risk assessing events being hosted by the Bank both internally and externally, particularly considering issues like invite lists, the landscape of current affairs, domestic and geopolitical risks, and location. Investigating and making decisions and or recommendations on referrals into the threat inbox of individuals who may pose a risk to the Bank and its people. Supporting the risk assessment and mitigation of Bank staff and or specific teams that may be at a heighten risk due to their seniority, areas of work, public exposure. This role requires analytical skills, keen attention to detail, and the ability to react promptly to potential threats. The analyst works proactively to develop and implement strategies that minimise risks and ensure a secure environment. Role Description This role sits within the Bank’s Personnel Security function, helping protect the Bank of England, its people and its operations from insider, personal safety and security risks. The role focuses on assessing, managing and mitigating risks linked to business travel, working from abroad, Bank-hosted or attended events, public-facing colleagues and referrals relating to individuals who may pose a risk to the Bank or its people. The successful candidate will combine strong judgement, analytical ability, attention to detail and clear communication. They will monitor global and domestic security developments, assess threats and vulnerabilities, provide practical advice, and support proportionate mitigations in line with the Bank’s risk appetite. Key Responsibilities Conduct comprehensive security risk assessments to Bank personal. Making informed recommendations on how to manage those risks and where appropriate escalate issues. This includes but is not limited to: Travel overseas which would include pre and post travel briefings with tailored security recommendations. Offer colleagues support during travel emergencies, liaising with travel risk management provider, insurers, brokers, local authorities, and third-party security providers. Conduct risk assessments for events attended and or hosted by Bank colleagues. Personal security risk assessments, providing recommendations, and delivering mitigations for Bank colleagues (typically at a senior level) and or specific teams that may be at a heighten risk. Monitor and analyse threats, vulnerabilities, and relevant incidents that could pose a risk to our travellers or events, such as: Crime, terrorism, political instability, current affairs, activism, natural disasters, and health risks. Actively support the develop, implementation, and updating of safety and security policies, procedures, and guidance that is proportionate and in line with the Bank’s organisational risk appetite. Actively support the Bank’s security education program. Professionally represent the Bank and collaborate with internal and external stakeholders, including other central banks, law enforcement, emergency services etc. Support the Banks counter eaves dropping / electronic monitoring activity, including the conduct sweeps to identify devices of concern. Role Requirements Minimum Criteria Recent experience making evidence-based security risk decisions, including assessing threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact and appropriate mitigations. Proven experience conducting either interviews, briefings and or structured information-gathering in a security, investigative or risk context. Experience of gathering and analysing information from various sources, such as security, geopolitical, travel, events, to inform risk assessments, recommendations or operational decisions. Experience of communicating clearly and confidently with stakeholders, including senior colleagues, while handling sensitive information with discretion. Able to handle sensitive information discreetly and securely. Essential Criteria Experience of in one of more of the areas of: travel security, event security, executive protection, or physical/personnel security. Demonstrable ability to produce clear, accurate written advice, reports and recommendations for varied audiences, including senior stakeholders. Proven attention to detail, with evidence of identifying relevant risks, inconsistencies and information gaps. Track record of managing busy workloads, prioritising competing demands and escalating issues appropriately with limited direction. Clear evidence of building trusted working relationships across internal teams and external partners, representing the Bank professionally and with discretion. Desirable Criteria Experience of or qualifications in residential security and of counter-eavesdropping / technical surveillance counter measures or NACE-accredited qualification. Ability to support development of policies, procedures, guidance, training, or awareness material in a practical and accessible way. item.title: Senior Benchmarks Supervision Associate
item.description: Job Title: Senior Benchmarks Supervision Associate Division: Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC) Department: Infrastructure and Exchanges Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £67,200 and London £59,200 to £73,800 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via steve.christopher@fca.org.uk . Your internal recruitment contact is Iona Magee via iona.magee@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK. We are currently seeking a skilled individual to join the Benchmarks and Credit Rating Agencies Supervision team within the Capital Markets Department. The Capital Markets Department sits within SPC division at the FCA and is responsible for both benchmark and credit rating agencies supervision and policy. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). The Benchmarks and Credit Ratings Supervision Team is responsible for supervising UK-regulated benchmark administrators and CRAs in line with the applicable regulatory requirements and the FCA’s Approach to Supervision. Benchmark administrators produce benchmarks that are used across financial markets. Where they perform this role effectively, market participants can rely on accurate and representative measures of underlying market activity. CRAs play a key role in providing an assessment of the creditworthiness of governments, corporates and other issuers of securities. Where they perform this role effectively, investors are well-informed on the risks of investing in these assets and hence, capital is more efficiently allocated. These outcomes contribute particularly to the FCA’s statutory objective for market integrity and its consumer protection objective. Role responsibilities Build trusted supervisory relationships with benchmark administrators, using constructive challenge and direct engagement to bring about positive change and effective regulatory outcomes Oversee strategic supervisory initiatives and engage with senior executives to improve governance, controls, methodologies and risk management practices Develop specialist expertise across a diverse portfolio of benchmarks, from globally significant indices to those supporting key sectors of the UK economy Identify, assess and respond to emerging market risks, applying sound judgement to deliver proportionate interventions that enhance market integrity and confidence Partner with colleagues across the FCA to bring together diverse insights, shape supervisory priorities and inform key regulatory decisions Collaborate with UK and international regulatory partners to address complex market issues and help deliver fair, effective and resilient financial markets Share expertise, present insights and contribute to a collaborative learning culture, enhancing the FCA’s supervisory effectiveness while building skills and experience for future leadership opportunities Skills required Minimum: Prior experience of working in a regulatory and/or financial services sector with professional experience related to indices and benchmarks Prior experience of working with the key risks related to indices and the wider financial ecosystem Prior experience in applying diagnostic skills, whether gained in industry, legal and/or financial services Essential: Good understanding of benchmark administrators’ business models, core processes and the potential risks associated with benchmark administration activities Demonstrated ability to lead and deliver projects effectively within agreed timelines while managing multiple priorities Effective verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present clear, concise and well-reasoned arguments to a range of stakeholders Ability to make informed and timely decisions, acting on own initiative to identify key issues, navigate complexity and escalate matters where appropriate Well-developed organisational skills, with the ability to balance competing priorities and manage changing demands effectively Flexible and responsive approach, with the ability to adjust to changing requirements and adapt working styles to meet evolving business needs Ability to work collaboratively, supporting colleagues and contributing to the successful delivery of shared objectives Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Timeline: Job advert close: 11th October 2026 at Midnight CV Review/Shortlist: 13th October 2026 Interviews: w/c 19th October 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time
